Subject: Dedicated capacity options for upcoming trial

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the intro over the call today. To recap our needs: Apollo Bio will run a 6-month clinical NLP pilot starting mid-May. Expected steady-state is ~70 requests/minute (most are short, ~300 tokens in/out) with 2 peak windows (up to 250 reqs/min for ~45 minutes) during batch processing. We need a predictable unit cost and a reserve that avoids queueing during peaks.

Primary asks:
- A phased reservation we can commit to as usage ramps (pilot -> validation -> production).
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs required for our SLA (99th pct latency targets).
- A pricing illustration (monthly reserved fee + overage) and a short ramp schedule.

I'm attaching the workload sample and a short latency SLO doc. Can you send a proposal with 2–3 reservation options we can evaluate?

Appreciate it —
Ava

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for upcoming trial

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the details and the workload sample. Attached is a concise set of reservation options designed to be easy to compare. High-level summary below — full numbers in the attached PDF and cost model spreadsheet.

Option A — Pilot-focused (lower up-front):
- Phase 1 (pilot): 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for months 1–2.
- Phase 2 (validation): scale to 24 GPUs month 3–4 (burst to 32 for short windows).
- Phase 3 (prod): evaluate moving to 48 GPUs month 5+ based on consumption.
- Contract: 12-month term optional; month-to-month for the first 3 months with 60-day minimum thereafter.
- Minimum guarantee: none in pilot, but recommend converting to a 16-GPU minimum on conversion to production to avoid preemption in your peak windows.

Option B — Balanced commitment (recommended for predictable latency):
- Phase 1: 16 GPUs reserved start (covers steady-state + headroom).
- Phase 2: automatic ramp to 32 GPUs after month 2 once usage crosses threshold; 64 GPUs available as a contracted ramp by month 6.
- Minimum guaranteed: 16 GPUs throughout contract.

Option C — Aggressive reserved path (best for heavy peak windows):
- Start at 32 GPUs reserved, scale to 64 by month 3. Minimum guaranteed 32.

Key operational notes:
- We support KV/prefix caching and per-customer routing so effective capacity can be higher than raw GPUs for some workloads.
- Autoscale burst is available for short peaks (billing as overage).
- We can set per-route SLOs and fallback to a cost-savvy variant (quantized) to prevent failed requests during extreme spikes.

I'm looping in Dylan (solutions) and Marissa (SE) to validate the ramp timings and the recommended minimum guarantees for your SLOs. Attached: APOLLO_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf, cost_model_apollo.xlsx.

Next step: can you confirm target go-live window (you said mid-May) and whether procurement prefers a single committed PO or staged purchase orders?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Final commercial summary: tiered reservation and ramp plan (proposal attached)

Hi Ava (and procurement team),

Thanks again for the collaboration — based on the workload sample and internal engineering feedback we've drafted a final commercial summary and an implementation ramp that we think aligns with your SLA and budget constraints. Key points below; full terms and numbers are in the attached APOLLO_Dedicated_Summary.docx and the cost model.

Summary (agreed recommendation):
- Contract form: 12-month reserved commitment with a phased ramp and early conversion credits for pilot months.
- Minimum guaranteed capacity: 16 GPUs reserved for the life of the contract (ensures no queueing during typical peaks).
- Phased ramp schedule:
  * Phase 0 (pilot, May 10 start): 8 reserved GPUs active immediately (pilot discount applied).
  * Phase 1 (validation, target Jun 15): automatically convert to 16 reserved GPUs (this is the contractual minimum).
  * Phase 2 (scale, target Aug 1): ramp to 32 reserved GPUs if usage thresholds (80% sustained over 2 weeks) are met.
  * Optional Phase 3 (production peak, by Nov): bump to 64 GPUs via an agreed-on amendment.
- Burst/autoscale: Short bursts to 64 GPUs available (metered as overage). We recommend a 20-minute continuous burst cap without pre-approval; longer bursts require notification.
- Fallbacks: quantized model variant available for non-critical routes; we can route 15% of low-priority traffic to quantized variant during extreme spikes.

Commercials (high-level):
- Reserved base fee: see attached (tiered pricing by GPU band).
- Overage: per-GPU-minute metering for bursts beyond reserved capacity.
- Credits: pilot months are partially credited against first-quarter reserved fees if you convert to a 12-month contract within 45 days.

Operational items we need from you to finalize contract:
1) Confirmation of PO cadence (single PO vs staged POs).
2) Procurement contact for DocuSign.
3) Any required security attachments (we will provide SOC 2 appendix).

Links and next steps:

- Proposal folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ApoProposalDriveLink
- DocuSign envelope (prepped): https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/0A1B2C3D4E

If that looks good I can route the DocuSign and we can target May 10 pilot activation. Happy to hop on another 30-min call this week to walk the procurement team through the ramp and billing.
